title: Concurrency and Mutable State in Servlets
platform_conditions: Jakarta/Javax servlet containers (Tomcat, Jetty, WebSphere); the container creates ONE servlet instance serving all requests concurrently
security_mechanism: The servlet specification keeps a single instance per servlet, so every instance field is shared by all concurrent requests: a currentUser field written by one request is read by another, letting a victim inherit an attacker's identity or vice versa. SimpleDateFormat stores intermediate parsing state in its instance and corrupts output or throws under concurrency; HashMap without synchronization loses updates and (in older JDKs) can loop under concurrent resize. A check-then-act pattern on an instance field ('if (this.session == null) create') races two requests into double initialization with mismatched credentials.

source_sink_clues.source: Concurrent HTTP requests handled by the same servlet/filter/bean instance; per-request values stored in instance fields.
source_sink_clues.sink: Mutable instance fields in HttpServlet/Filter/singletons holding request or identity data; shared SimpleDateFormat/HashMap instances used from request threads; check-then-act sequences on instance state

tracking_guards: Check that per-request values live in local variables or request/session attributes rather than instance fields; check shared utility instances are replaced by ThreadLocal or immutable/thread-safe types (DateTimeFormatter, ConcurrentHashMap); check check-then-act sequences are atomic under a lock orCAS.
not_candidate_when: The fields are read-only after container initialization (safe publication with final/initialization-on-demand), the servlet is explicitly single-threaded (SingleThreadModel-era or one instance per request), shared state is confined to ConcurrentHashMap/Atomic types, or the field holds immutable configuration only.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: public class UserServlet extends HttpServlet { private String currentUser; }
synthetic_safe_example: public class UserServlet extends HttpServlet { /* use local variables */ }
public_references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition') — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
